ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Odontoid classification: 4

An older patient with a type II odontoid fracture has persistent separation and no progressive healing on follow-up. The clinician reassesses stability and treatment goals. Which healing complication is particularly relevant to this fracture location?

  1. Post-traumatic osteoarthritis
  2. Acute compartment syndrome
  3. Nonunion
  4. Joint stiffness
  5. Osteonecrosis
Answer and explanation

Nonunion

Persistent failure of fracture healing requires assessment of stability, biology, infection and patient factors.

Option explanations

Nonunion: Persistent failure of fracture healing requires assessment of stability, biology, infection and patient factors.

Joint stiffness: Capsular contracture, adhesions and prolonged immobilization can restrict motion after injury. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Osteonecrosis: Disruption of blood supply can lead to death and collapse of an injured bony segment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Post-traumatic osteoarthritis: Articular incongruity or cartilage damage can cause later degenerative joint changes. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Acute compartment syndrome: Rising compartment pressure impairs perfusion; escalating pain and pain on passive stretch require urgent assessment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
